personas.name: Marcus Bell
personas.location: Atlanta, GA (Fulton County, Midtown loft; physically works 4 days/wk at a WeWork in West Midtown)
personas.day_in_life_pain: Marcus is a senior product designer turned independent contractor. In May 2025 he landed a 6-month contract with a SaaS company headquartered in San Francisco. The client is a CA LLC; they sent him a 1099-NEC for $58,400 in November. He lives in Atlanta, has a Georgia sales-tax account for an old side hustle, and has never had a CA nexus question before. June 15 has passed; he missed Q2 federal estimated (owed $4,180, paid $0) and didn't know he had to file a CA 540-ES because his only CA connection was one client's mailing address. He's now staring at three separate quarterly obligations he didn't plan for: federal 1040-ES (federal $1,000 threshold), Georgia IT-560 (GA requires quarterly if >$500 expected liability), and California 540-ES (CA triggers at $500 of CA-source income). Three forms, three due dates that drift (CA 540-ES Q2 is June 15, federal is the same, but GA IT-560 Q2 is also June 15, and the math differs because CA is a high-tax state with the 1.1% Mental Health Services Tax surcharge above $1M and a 9.3% top marginal rate vs GA's 5.39% flat). He's using QuarterPilot which only does federal + his home state; it doesn't know about his CA nexus. His CPA charges $385/hr; Marcus has 3 hours of billable time eaten by the question. He wants one app that says 'Marcus, here is what you owe each state this quarter, here are the three forms, here are the three deadlines, here is what happens if you underpay each one (8% annualized federal, 5% CA, 4% GA).' He wants to share that with his mom (who is on his bank account as a co-signer) and his CPA. The current workaround is: he googles '1040-ES calculator' + '540-ES calculator' + 'GA IT-560 calculator', runs three numbers, pays the federal via IRS Direct Pay, pays CA via FTB Web Pay, and never gets around to the GA. He will owe an underpayment penalty on the GA. He is the multi-state 1099 nexus wedge made concrete.
personas.current_workaround: QuarterPilot (federal + GA only, no CA), 3 separate state tax calculators, IRS Direct Pay + CA FTB Web Pay + GA DOR ITSU, CPA at $385/hr. Average time-to-quarterly-completion: 6 hours across 2 weekends. He has no consolidated 'all-my-states' view, no state-threshold pre-screen (does a new client in MA trigger another quarterly?), no shareable summary for his CPA, no Sunday digest that says 'Q3 estimated is due September 15.'
personas.wishlist: A single app that (1) tracks his multi-state nexus as he adds clients (state-by-state, with the state-specific trigger threshold auto-loaded: $500 CA, $300 NY, $1,000 federal, $0 in 7 no-income-tax states, $5,000+ in most others), (2) generates a quarterly 1040-ES + state form set for each active nexus state, (3) sends a Sunday 'Q-due' digest 10 days before each deadline with the actual numbers, (4) produces a printable year-end Schedule C + state return pre-fill, (5) lets him share a private 'my quarterly tax plan' link with his CPA or his mom (read-only).

personas.name: Rosa Delgado
personas.location: Hialeah, FL (Miami-Dade, 22-seat Cuban cafe 'Cafecito Rosa' on W 49th St, 9 employees, husband helps on weekends)
personas.household_income: $1,420,000 gross revenue / ~$78,000 owner draw (cafe net margin ~5.5% after food/labor/rent; husband is an HVAC tech, $62,000 W-2)
personas.day_in_life_pain: Rosa took out a $145,000 'merchant cash advance' in October 2023 from a non-Yellowstone funder (let me call them 'FastFunds Capital') after a slow post-hurricane quarter. The contract is written as a 'purchase of future receivables' at a 1.32 factor (she pays back $191,400). Daily ACH debits are $890/day, 7 days a week, drawn from her restaurant's business checking at Truist. The contract was 14 pages of dense legalese; she signed it on a Wednesday between the lunch rush and the dinner prep. She did not read it. She has since learned three things she didn't know on signing day: (1) the contract has a 'reconciliation clause' on page 9 that says the funder MUST adjust her daily payment if her revenue drops 30%+ month-over-month — the funder has never honored it despite her revenue dropping in May 2025 and February 2026; (2) the contract has a 'cross-default' clause on page 11 that says defaulting on this MCA puts her in default on a $40,000 second MCA she also took with the same funder; (3) the contract has a 'confession of judgment' clause (page 13) authorizing the funder to enter a NY Supreme Court judgment against her without notice. She has not missed a payment. She has $34,000 remaining on the larger MCA. On January 22, 2025, NY AG Letitia James announced a $1.065B settlement with Yellowstone Capital canceling $534M in MCA debt for 18,000 merchants; Rosa's funder was NOT Yellowstone so she got nothing. On December 19, 2025, NY Governor Hochul signed the FAIR Act (effective Feb 17 2026), extending NY GBL § 349 to cover 'unfair' and 'abusive' practices against businesses — but Rosa is in Florida, not NY, and the FAIR Act's protections for her are indirect at best. On February 20, 2026, a federal bankruptcy court in SDNY (In re Greenwich Retail Group) ruled that MCA agreements with implied APRs of 65-132% can be recharacterized as loans and the prior payments recovered as fraudulent transfers — but Rosa is not in bankruptcy. She has paid $1,490/day in cumulative debits for 30 months and is now $1,490 short of the $191,400 total. She has $7,200 in her business account. The 'debt relief' company that cold-called her in March 2025 quoted $4,800 upfront to 'negotiate' her MCA; she almost paid. She is the post-Yellowstone, post-FAIR-Act restaurant owner who is mathematically still in the trap because her funder was one step removed from the canceled names. Her daily workaround is: check the Truist balance at 6 am, hope the $890 debit doesn't overdraft, make payroll Friday, repeat. There is no consumer-side tool that says 'Rosa, your MCA may be recharacterizable as a loan under NY law and as a violation of the new FAIR Act' or 'Rosa, demand reconciliation in writing, certified mail, here's the template.' She has $34,000 left to pay under a contract that may be unenforceable; she doesn't know.
personas.current_workaround: Read the contract once in March 2025 after a cousin mentioned Yellowstone; Truist business banker won't help (Truist does not advise on third-party MCAs); local SCORE mentor recommended 'just pay it'; a $4,800 'debt relief' company nearly got her money in March 2025; she googled 'merchant cash advance help' and got 3 law-firm ads and 8 debt-relief ads. No consumer-side tool that ingests the MCA, computes the effective APR, surfaces the reconciliation clause, and tells her whether her specific contract is challengeable under FAIR Act / NY Penal Law § 190.40 / In re Greenwich Retail.

pain_signals.signal: Multi-state 1099 quarterly estimated tax: federal $1,000 threshold + 50 state-specific forms (CA 540-ES triggers at $500, NY IT-2105 at $300, GA IT-560 at $500, 7 no-income-tax states at $0) + 4 federal deadlines (Apr 15 / Jun 15 / Sep 15 / Jan 15) + per-state underpayment penalty rates (federal 8% annualized, CA 5%, GA 4%) + 25-30% set-aside rule, with no single consumer-side app that tracks nexus as clients are added
personas_affected: Rosa Delgado (the cafe owner, Schedule C filer; secondary)
pain_signals.current_workaround: Open 3 separate state tax calculators + 1 federal calculator; manually reconcile per-state thresholds; QuarterPilot covers only federal + home state; CPA at $385/hr if you can afford it. Net result: missed CA underpayment penalty in the typical case, missed GA entirely, no shared view with the spouse or CPA, no proactive 'Q3 is in 30 days' reminder.
pain_signals.why_now_2026: 1099-NEC reporting threshold raised to $2,000 (was $600) starting 2026 — but the platform-side 1099-K threshold dropped to $600 for Uber/Lyft/DoorDash/Instacart in 2026, meaning gig income is more visible to the IRS than ever. The number of multi-state 1099 filers is structurally growing because remote-work-from-anywhere arrangements let a designer in GA do $58K of work for a CA LLC without the CA LLC withholding a cent. QuarterPilot exists but only covers one state; no app on the market handles the 'I added a new client in a new state — does it trigger a new quarterly?' wedge.

pain_signals.signal: MCA reconciliation clause buried in contracts + cross-default stacking + confession of judgment + post-Yellowstone residual trap for 18,000+ non-Yellowstone merchants; NY FAIR Act effective Feb 17 2026 + In re Greenwich Retail Feb 20 2026 + NY Penal Law 190.40 25% usury cap are 3 freshly-unlocked defenses with no consumer-side tool to surface them
personas_affected: Rosa Delgado (22-seat cafe owner with $145K FastFunds MCA at 1.32 factor; primary persona)
Marcus Bell (sole-prop with $0 MCA exposure, but $7K line of credit on his AmEx; the reconciliation-clause concept generalizes to all SMB credit contracts)
pain_signals.current_workaround: Restaurant owner reads the contract once in March 2025; Truist business banker declines to advise on a third-party MCA; SCORE mentor says 'just pay it'; 'debt relief' company quotes $4,800 upfront to negotiate (this is itself a known scam); 3 law-firm ads + 8 debt-relief ads in Google results; no consumer-side tool ingests the MCA, computes effective APR (true cost = factor rate compounded daily, often 60-130% APR), surfaces the reconciliation clause, or maps the contract against FAIR Act / NY Penal Law § 190.40 / In re Greenwich Retail.
pain_signals.why_now_2026: Three inflection points in 14 months: (1) Yellowstone settlement Jan 22 2025 canceled $534M for 18,000 merchants — leaving 100,000+ other merchants with non-Yellowstone funders in a 'why not me?' vacuum; (2) NY FAIR Act signed Dec 19 2025, effective Feb 17 2026, extends GBL § 349 to 'unfair' + 'abusive' business practices — first time businesses have AG-enforceable consumer-style protections; (3) In re Greenwich Retail Group Feb 20 2026 (SDNY 2026 WL 482170) allowed the 'waiver-as-fraudulent-transfer' theory to survive motions to dismiss, opening bankruptcy-court unwinding of MCA payments. None of these defenses is surfaced in any consumer-side tool. The $4,800 'debt relief' scam is a known corollary and an opportunity for a 'don't pay them, here's the actual letter to send' alternative.

pain_signals.signal: SBA 7(a) loan closing is a 30-90 day 5-stage process (application 1-2 weeks / underwriting 2-4 weeks / SBA review 5-21 business days / closing prep 1-3 weeks / closing 1 day) with 504 adding a CDC and a debenture-sale wait (60-120 days total), real estate adding 4-6 weeks for appraisal + environmental, and SBA Express as a 36-hour fast path up to $500K — and there is no consumer-side companion that walks a first-time SMB borrower through the 5 stages with a stage-by-stage checklist
personas_affected: Marcus Bell (designer; may seek SBA 7(a) Express for $80K working capital in 2027 if his contract is renewed; secondary)
Rosa Delgado (cafe owner; may seek SBA 7(a) to consolidate the remaining $34K MCA; secondary)
pain_signals.current_workaround: Borrower goes to one SBA-preferred lender, gets a 14-document PDF checklist, scrambles to gather 2 years of personal + business tax returns + interim P&L + personal financial statement + debt schedule + 3 months of bank statements; the lender's portal holds the checklist with no view for the borrower; no consumer-side app counts 'day 23 of 60-90, you should be in SBA review now' or surfaces 'you can pay $500 extra to use a PLP lender and cut 20-30% off the timeline' or 'real estate adds 4-6 weeks, plan for that.' Lenders don't tell borrowers about SBA Express (36-hour, $500K) because the lender makes more on a 7(a) Standard; borrowers don't know to ask.
pain_signals.why_now_2026: Average SBA 7(a) close time is 60-90 days in 2026; 504 is 60-120 days; real estate 7(a) is 75-90 days. PLP lender delegation cuts 20-30% off the timeline but is not advertised. SBA Express (36-hour, $500K cap) is the obvious fast path most first-time borrowers don't know exists. The 2026 wedge is that lenders' portals own the checklist; the borrower is the last to know what stage they're in. Closest existing corpus record is `payroll-picket` (B2B Davis-Bacon compliance) — adjacent mechanism (M9 deadline state machine) but completely different domain (prevailing wage, not SBA closing).

pain_signals.signal: SAM.gov activation is 7-15 business days (IRS TIN match 2-5 days + CAGE 3-7 days) with EIN-name-mismatch as the #1 30-day delay trap, PO box as primary address rejection, and annual renewals that lapse silently; on top of that, federal set-aside applications (8(a) 90-120 days, WOSB 10-15 days, HUBZone ongoing with 35% resident + 10-hr/wk rule, SDVOSB VetCert Dec 2024 deadline) were radically restructured by the Jan 16 2025 SBA final rule + the federal court ruling that struck 8(a) 'presumed disadvantage' (admissions dropped 550 in 2024 to 66 in 2025)
personas_affected: (not primary for Marcus or Rosa; this is a secondary persona) a service-disabled-veteran-owned cybersecurity firm in Tampa FL with a UEI already; first-time 8(a) applicant after the 2025 rule change; needs the social-disadvantage narrative template + the 90-120 day calendar + the day-300 renewal reminder
pain_signals.current_workaround: Procurement federal consultants charge $2K-$15K to walk an applicant through MySBA Certifications; SBA Federal Service Desk at 866-606-8220 is free but averages 30+ minute hold; NAICS code selection is a 1,000-row dropdown with no side-by-side size-standard comparison; the social-disadvantage narrative (post the 2025 federal court ruling) is a free-text essay the SBA reviewer scores subjectively; HUBZone 35% resident + 10-hr/wk rule is computed manually from payroll records every 4 weeks pre-application.
pain_signals.why_now_2026: Three concurrent 2025-26 rule changes: (1) FAR 52.204-7 final rule Aug 7 2025 relaxed the continuous-SAM-registration requirement, but only for solicitations issued after Aug 7 — older solicitations still require it, so contractors still have to monitor it; (2) SBA final rule Jan 16 2025 made HUBZone 35% compliance rolling-12-month-from-award (not from application), 10-hr/wk minimum, 90-day residency (down from 180); (3) federal court ruling struck 8(a) 'presumed disadvantage' so every 8(a) applicant must now write a narrative; admissions collapsed from 550 (2024) to 66 (2025). SBA cleared 2,700 VetCert backlog in early 2026. The wedge is the post-2025 complexity: a small business owner who qualified for 8(a) under the old rules now needs a narrative, a NAICS strategy, a 90-120 day calendar, and an HR-system that can produce 4-week payroll snapshots. No consumer-side tool handles the bundling.

pain_signals.signal: ERC post-VDP closure Nov 22 2024 leaves 1.2M unprocessed claims + 30,000 IRS clawback letters in the mail (targeting $1B+ in errant claims) + the IRS Withdrawal Program still open (Form 15434 alternative) for any taxpayer whose claim hasn't been paid; the second-VDP took only 48 applications vs 2,609 for the first VDP because the program was poorly publicized and many recipients didn't know they were ineligible
personas_affected: (not primary for Marcus or Rosa; this is a secondary persona) a 12-employee dental practice in Orlando FL that received a $214,000 ERC refund in Sept 2023 and just received a 30,000-letter-batch IRS clawback notice in May 2026; the practice's CPA quoted $6,500 to handle the response; the practice owner is shopping for a cheaper path
pain_signals.current_workaround: Call a CPA ($2,500-$15,000 for ERC Withdrawal or clawback response); use the IRS Document Upload Tool with Form 15434 (free but a 14-page application); or ignore the letter and hope the IRS doesn't escalate. Many 'ERC mill' marketing firms that originally helped the owner file now charge $5K-$25K to unwind it. The IRS Taxpayer Advocate reports 1.2M unprocessed claims as of Oct 26 2024 with no status updates and no expected timeline.
pain_signals.why_now_2026: The 30,000-letter batch (May 2026, $1B+ target) is the IRS's second-largest clawback effort after the 2023 batch. The second VDP closed Nov 22 2024; the Withdrawal Program is still open. The Taxpayer Advocate flagged in Dec 2024 that 1.2M claims remain unprocessed. The wedge: a small business owner who got an ERC refund in 2023 has 3 options (ignore, withdraw, respond to clawback), needs to pick one, and has no consumer-side tool that classifies the letter and walks them through the right path. Closest existing corpus record is `denialpilot` (insurance denial appeal) — adjacent mechanism (M7 evidence packet, M9 deadline clock) but a different domain (ERC + IRS clawback, not insurance).

idea_hypotheses.name: MCADetector
idea_hypotheses.one_liner: Snap your MCA contract. Get the effective APR, the buried reconciliation clause, the cross-default trap, and a one-tap 'demand reconciliation' letter post-NY-FAIR-Act.
idea_hypotheses.target_user: US SMB owner (cafe, salon, retail, contractor) carrying an outstanding merchant cash advance with a daily/weekly ACH debit who is not sure whether the contract is enforceable, post-FAIR-Act or pre-FAIR-Act.
idea_hypotheses.mechanism: M5 (share/photo/PDF intake of the MCA contract, plus a one-tap photo of the bank statement showing the daily debit) + M6 (entitlement/rule reference: NY Penal Law § 190.40 25% usury cap, NY GBL § 349 + FAIR Act Feb 17 2026, In re Greenwich Retail Group Feb 20 2026 SDNY, FTC RCG Advances ban, NY CPLR 3218 confessions-of-judgment amendment Aug 30 2019, NY AG Yellowstone settlement Jan 22 2025) + M7 (evidence packet: a printable 'Your MCA Audit' PDF with effective APR computation, the cited page numbers for reconciliation / cross-default / confession-of-judgment clauses, and a certified-mail-ready reconciliation demand letter) + M9 (deadline state machine: a clock for the 30-day reconciliation-demand response window + the 1-year statute-of-limitations on a fraudulent-transfer claim if in bankruptcy + the 5-year limitations under NY GBL § 349) + M25 (authority boundary: labels 'this contract MAY be challengeable under [cited law]' not 'this contract is illegal').
idea_hypotheses.payer: $9.99/mo or $49 one-time audit; B2B referral fee to MCA-defense law firms (Delancey Street / Mike Assad / DHC bankruptcy group) for the 5-10% of users who need a lawyer; future B2B tier for Truist / Chase Business Banking to surface MCA risk in their SMB dashboards.
idea_hypotheses.mechanism_lineage: M5 from SnapInvoice / JobNote / pet-fairquote (tick 19); M6 from payroll-picket (B2B regulatory rule reference) and pet-fairquote's humane-society / CareCredit rule reference; M7 from denialpilot (insurance evidence packet); M9 from docket-guard (deadline clock); M25 (authority boundary) is the explicit differentiator vs the $4,800 'debt relief' scam. The 'MCA is a loan' recharacterization is the inverse of PetFairQuote's 'vet estimate may be above median' — both are authority-boundary signals that change the consumer's leverage without the consumer hiring a lawyer. The mechanism family is 'consumer-side regulatory unlock,' parallel to the tick-12 B2B regulatory tick (payroll-picket, compass-rosetta).
idea_hypotheses.primary_risk: (1) The 'MCA may be challengeable' framing is a regulated legal-advice-adjacent claim; must be paired with a strict M25 authority-boundary label and a non-lawyer 'this is not legal advice' disclosure, or the app exposes itself to UPL. (2) The MCA-funder industry may lobby state legislatures to explicitly preempt consumer-side contract analysis. (3) The Yellowstone-window already closed for the largest cohort; the addressable market is the 100K+ non-Yellowstone merchants whose funders are still active, plus the tens of thousands of merchants who missed the VDP because they didn't know they were eligible. Kill trigger: <1,000 contract submissions in 60 days OR a state UPL opinion blocking consumer-side MCA contract analysis OR a major funder (FastFunds / OnDeck / BlueVine / Kabbage) ships a free 'reconciliation-rights' portal for their own borrowers within 90 days.
idea_hypotheses.source_overlap_check: No name/one_liner collision with the off-limits list. Closest corpus records: `payroll-picket` (B2B Davis-Bacon, different regulatory domain) and `denialpilot` (insurance denial appeal, adjacent M7 evidence-packet mechanism but different domain). The MCA wedge is genuinely greenfield in the corpus. The consumer-side 'is this contract legal' framing is the inverse of `billdr` (hospital bill dispute) and `otddecoder` (auto dealer OTD decode) — both are 'is the bill fair?' products; MCADetector is 'is the credit contract fair?' and the regulatory unlock (FAIR Act + Greenwich Retail) is unique to 2026.

idea_hypotheses.name: QuarterNest
idea_hypotheses.one_liner: Track your multi-state 1099 nexus; get a per-state quarterly estimate + form set + Sunday 'Q-due' digest; share with your CPA in one link.
idea_hypotheses.target_user: US 1099-NEC / sole-prop / freelancer with income from 2+ states (designer, copywriter, consultant, agency-of-one, remote contractor for a CA/NY/MA client while living in TX/FL/GA), 50K-$200K AGI, no full-time bookkeeper.
idea_hypotheses.mechanism: M19 (multi-form synthesis: federal 1040-ES + state-specific estimated-tax form per active nexus state — CA 540-ES, NY IT-2105, GA IT-560, etc., with the right per-state threshold and the right per-state underpayment-penalty rate) + M6 (entitlement/rule reference: federal $1,000 trigger, CA $500 trigger, NY $300 trigger, GA $500 trigger, 7 no-income-tax states at $0 trigger, per-state set-aside percentage 25-30%) + M1 (Sunday/quarterly ritual digest: 'Q3 is due September 15 — here's what you owe each of your 3 nexus states' with the actual computed numbers) + M24 (accepted handoff: 'I sent this to my CPA' or 'I paid federal 1040-ES via Direct Pay' or 'I paid CA 540-ES via FTB Web Pay' — explicit confirmation of which state's payment landed) + M25 (authority boundary: explicitly labels 'computed from IRS + [state] FTB published rules; not a substitute for a CPA').
idea_hypotheses.payer: $4.99/mo or $29/yr consumer subscription; $9.99/mo 'QuarterNest + CPA' tier with a share-link and quarterly PDF export; future B2B tier for accountants managing 20+ 1099 clients; sponsored placement of the IRS Direct Pay + state DOR payment links (no affiliate revenue, just UX).
idea_hypotheses.mechanism_lineage: M19 from `multistate-form-synthesizer-funeral` (B2B funeral, passed_scope) and `cottage-exemption-tracker` (B2B cottage-food, passed_market) — both vertical narrows of the same M19 mechanism, but neither addresses the 1099/sole-prop quarterly wedge. M6 from `payroll-picket` (Davis-Bacon rule reference) and `compass-rosetta` (B2B regulatory digest). M1 from `compass-rosetta` (weekly digest) and `energysheet` (monthly ritual). M24 from `rental-turnover-ready-ack` and `pet-farewell-kit` accepted-handoff. The 'multi-state nexus' is the explicit differentiator vs QuarterPilot (single-state) and the existing `gig-1099-deposit-reconciliation` (NetCheck, parked, low hackathon fit, focused on 1099-K vs bank reconciliation — different wedge, different season, parked explicitly because of tax-season timing; but QuarterNest IS a tax-season product, so NetCheck's parked-due-to-season rationale is irrelevant to QuarterNest's eval).
idea_hypotheses.primary_risk: (1) QuarterPilot already exists for single-state. A multi-state extension has to ship before QuarterPilot adds multi-state, OR QuarterPilot ships a multi-state tier within 90 days. (2) The 'per-state threshold' table is volatile (CA, NY, GA adjust; new state income-tax triggers happen — e.g., the AR, MS, and AL 2023-2025 phase-downs) so M21 per-state rules database maintenance is non-trivial; mitigated by an explicit 'verified for 2026 tax year, check with your CPA for material changes' label. (3) IRS Direct Pay + 50 state payment portals is a routing job; if any state changes its payment URL, the link breaks. (4) The product is a CPA substitute for the 80% of freelancers who can't afford one; the 20% who already have a CPA may see it as redundant. Kill trigger: <2,000 multi-state active users in 90 days OR QuarterPilot ships a multi-state tier at the same price OR TurboTax Live / Keeper Tax ship a quarterly-state tax product within 90 days.
idea_hypotheses.source_overlap_check: No name/one_liner collision with the off-limits list. Closest corpus record: `gig-1099-deposit-reconciliation` (NetCheck) — but NetCheck is parked specifically because it is about 1099-K vs bank reconciliation (a different quarterly pain, mostly Jan-April tax prep), not multi-state quarterly tax scheduling (a year-round ritual). Domain separation: NetCheck reconciles past income; QuarterNest schedules future quarterly payments. Different mechanism, different season, different state of decision. M19 multi-form-synthesis is the explicit lineage from `multistate-form-synthesizer-funeral` (passed_scope, B2B) and `cottage-exemption-tracker` (B2B) — QuarterNest is the B2C narrow of the same family.

idea_hypotheses.name: ClosingClock
idea_hypotheses.one_liner: A stage-by-stage SBA 7(a)/504 closing checklist with ETA, what to ask the lender, and a Sunday 'Day 47 of 60-90' digest. $6.99/mo during closing.
idea_hypotheses.target_user: US first-time SBA 7(a) or 504 borrower (small business owner seeking $50K-$5M working capital, equipment, or commercial real estate) who has never closed an SBA loan and is 0-90 days into a closing window.
idea_hypotheses.mechanism: M9 (deadline state machine: 5 stages — Application & Prequalification (1-2 weeks) / Document Collection (1-2 weeks) / Lender Underwriting (2-4 weeks) / SBA Review (5-21 business days) / Closing Prep & Funding (1-3 weeks) — with 504 adding a CDC and a debenture-sale wait that pushes to 60-120 days; PLP lender path cuts 20-30%; SBA Express 36-hour fast path up to $500K) + M1 (Sunday ritual digest: 'Day 47 of 60-90 — you should be in SBA review now; if you're not, here's the email to send your loan officer') + M6 (entitlement/rule reference: SBA SOP 50 10 (Lender Development Company), SBA Express guarantee fee schedule, PLP vs non-PLP delegation, 504 debenture sale calendar — second Tuesday of each month per CDC) + M24 (accepted handoff: borrower marks each lender request 'received and accepted' with a date; distinguishes 'I sent it' from 'they confirmed receipt') + M25 (authority boundary: 'based on SBA published timelines; PLP/non-PLP delegation, your lender's specific timing may vary').
idea_hypotheses.payer: $6.99/mo during the 30-120 day closing window (auto-cancels at 'Funded' status); $14.99/mo for an SBA Express fast-path tier; future B2B tier for SBA Preferred Lenders (Live Oak, Celtic Bank, Newtek) to put their checklist into the borrower's app and reduce 'where is my loan?' calls; CPA referral for the 5-10% of borrowers whose closing stalls and who need a workout advisor.
idea_hypotheses.mechanism_lineage: M9 from `docket-guard` (statute-of-limitations deadline clock, tick 18) — ClosingClock is the B2B/SMB narrow of the same deadline-state-machine mechanism, but for a 30-120 day window instead of a 1-10 year statute clock. M1 from `compass-rosetta` (weekly regulatory digest) and `energysheet` (monthly utility bill digest). M24 from `rental-turnover-ready-ack` accepted-handoff pattern. M6 from `payroll-picket` (B2B regulatory rule reference). The 'borrower-side checklist' is the inverse of `payroll-picket` (B2B employer-side prevailing-wage compliance) — ClosingClock is B2B/SMB borrower-side, not employer-side, and the regulatory surface (SBA SOPs + PLP delegation + debenture sale calendar) is unique. Closest corpus record: `credential-wall-small-employers` (license/COI tracking, different domain).
idea_hypotheses.primary_risk: (1) The lender's portal already has a checklist; ClosingClock is the borrower-side mirror. If a major SBA Preferred Lender (Live Oak, which is the largest 7(a) lender by dollar volume) ships a borrower-facing app with the same stage-by-stage view within 90 days, ClosingClock loses. (2) The 5-stage timeline has wide ranges (7(a) 30-90 days is a 60-day window) and the per-stage averages vary by lender, region, and loan amount; the M25 authority-boundary label has to be honest about this or the digest becomes a source of borrower frustration. (3) The TAM is small — SBA 7(a) originations are ~50,000 loans/yr at ~$45B total, and only first-time borrowers are the addressable wedge (repeat borrowers have their own checklist). Kill trigger: <500 active closing-window borrowers in 90 days OR Live Oak / Celtic Bank / Newtek ship a borrower-facing SBA tracker app within 90 days.
idea_hypotheses.source_overlap_check: No name/one_liner collision with the off-limits list. Closest corpus record: `payroll-picket` (Davis-Bacon B2B regulatory) — adjacent M9 mechanism, completely different domain. `docket-guard` (statute-of-limitations deadline clock) — adjacent M9 mechanism, different time scale (years vs months). `closinglens` (real estate closing decoder) — name similarity is a 1-word overlap ('closing'); domain is residential real estate wire fraud / closing disclosure, not SBA business-loan closing. Domain separation: ClosingClock is for SBA-guaranteed business loans ($50K-$5M, 30-120 day window, 5 stages); closinglens is for residential real estate purchases (15-60 day window, 1 closing). Different lender, different artifact, different regulator.

synthesis_verdict: Three ideas advance: MCADetector (primary), QuarterNest (secondary), ClosingClock (tertiary). All three pass the mock-hackathon lens (RevenueCat-eligible, 6-week buildable, weekly-ritual + shareable, crafted subscription). All three are B2C or B2C-flavoured-B2B and domain-separated from the off-limits list and the existing corpus records. MCADetector is the strongest single wedge — Yellowstone + FAIR Act + In re Greenwich Retail + the 30,000 IRS clawback letter wave all converge in 14 months to make 'consumer-side MCA contract analysis' a real 2026 wedge; the M25 authority-boundary label is the explicit guardrail vs the $4,800 'debt relief' scam. QuarterNest is the broadest TAM (every 1099 worker in a multi-state situation) but the most competed (QuarterPilot, Keeper Tax, TurboTax Live); its differentiator is the multi-state M19 narrow and the CPA-shareable link. ClosingClock is the narrowest TAM (50K SBA originations/yr, only first-timers) but the highest per-user value ($6.99/mo during a 30-120 day window where the borrower is anxious); its differentiator is the borrower-side mirror of the lender portal's checklist. All three ideas are weekly-ritual (MCADetector monthly digest for active MCAs; QuarterNest Sunday Q-due digest 4x/yr; ClosingClock Sunday Day-N-of-60-90 digest for the closing window). Primary risk across all three: state / federal regulator preemption (FAIR Act challenge from MCA industry, IRS rejection of self-filed Form 15434, SBA rule change that auto-renews SAM.gov for compliant entities). Recommend advancing all three to the corpus and parking the SAM.gov/ERC/Blue-Apricot/Sub-S wedges for future ticks.
